description: Engineer at least one alpha signal from non-price BTCUSDT futures microstructure data (volume, taker buy/sell, trade count) and evaluate it via IC, quantile spread, horizon decay, and subperiod robustness.
agent_prompt: Research a microstructure-based alpha on BTCUSDT futures using only non-price (volume / orderflow) features. Inputs at /workspace/data/: BTCUSDT_1d_2021_2024.csv, BTCUSDT_1h_2023_2024.csv, BTCUSDT_5m_2024Q4.csv. Each file contains columns including taker_buy_volume, taker_sell_volume, trade_count alongside OHLCV. Tasks: (1) engineer at least 3 candidate signals with explicit mathematical definitions documented at /workspace/output/signal_definitions.md (examples: taker buy/sell imbalance ratio, volume z-score residual after removing rolling mean, trade-count surprise, cross-timeframe orderflow divergence); (2) for each signal, evaluate predictive content vs forward 1d returns using: rank IC (mean and t-stat), top-vs-bottom quintile return spread (annualized), hit rate; write /workspace/output/signal_evaluation.csv with columns signal_name, ic_mean, ic_tstat, q5_q1_spread_ann, hit_rate; (3) horizon decay analysis — recompute IC at horizons {1d, 3d, 5d, 10d} and write /workspace/output/horizon_decay.csv (signal_name × horizon → IC); (4) subperiod robustness — split sample into 3 calendar periods and report per-period IC; write /workspace/output/subperiod_robustness.csv; (5) deployment constraints memo at /workspace/output/deployment_notes.md identifying execution cost sensitivity, signal decay speed, capacity, or stability concern for each signal, with quantitative evidence from steps 2-4.

required_capabilities: Engineer derived features from non-price microstructure data with explicit mathematical definitions
Evaluate signal quality using rank IC, quantile return spread, and hit rate
Analyze IC decay across multiple forward horizons
Identify deployment constraints supported by quantitative evidence
